strings.name: Andrej Karpathy
strings.summary: Born in Bratislava, Karpathy studied in Canada, researched neural networks and vision-language problems at Stanford and helped develop deep-learning teaching. He was an early OpenAI member, led Tesla’s Autopilot vision team and later returned to OpenAI. He founded Eureka Labs for AI-assisted education in 2024 and joined Anthropic’s pretraining team in 2026. His courses, code and explanations are also influential channels for researchers and developers.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; reviewed November 15, 2026. This is not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Works in computer vision, autonomous driving and large-language-model engineering, with broad influence through public technical teaching and industry practice.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: University of Toronto bachelor’s (2009); University of British Columbia master’s (2011); Stanford computer science doctorate.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Learning across vision and language
strings.highlights.h1.text: Researched neural-network applications in vision and language at Stanford and helped teach CS231n.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Research and public education
strings.highlights.h2.text: Explains deep learning through open code, courses and videos, connecting research practice with developer learning.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Joining Anthropic
strings.timeline.t1.text: Joined its pretraining team for large-scale model training, according to his announcement and company confirmation.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Founding Eureka Labs
strings.timeline.t2.text: Announced AI-assisted education combining teachers’ courses with AI teaching assistants.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Returning to OpenAI
strings.timeline.t3.text: Returned to the research organization and built a team for midtraining and synthetic data.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Joining Tesla
strings.timeline.t4.text: Became AI director, leading the Autopilot computer vision team.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Early OpenAI membership
strings.timeline.t5.text: Joined the newly established AI research organization as a research scientist.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Developing Stanford’s deep-learning course
strings.timeline.t6.text: Designed and led CS231n, teaching convolutional neural networks for vision.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Beginning Stanford doctoral research
strings.timeline.t7.text: Studied neural networks and the intersection of vision and natural language under Fei-Fei Li.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completing Toronto studies
strings.timeline.t8.text: Studied computing and physics, then researched learned control for simulated figures at UBC.
